questions.q: What is a "block" in a joined report?
options: A filter applied to the whole report
A single row in the report
One report's worth of columns and filters, shown side by side with the others
A chart embedded in the report
questions.explain: Each block is effectively its own report (its own columns and filters, possibly its own report type), displayed alongside the other blocks in one joined view.

questions.q: How many blocks can a single joined report contain?
options: Exactly 2
Up to 5
Unlimited
Up to 10
questions.explain: A joined report supports up to five blocks, each of the same or a different report type.

questions.q: What does "Group Across Blocks" do in a joined report's Outline panel?
options: Deletes a block
Merges all blocks into a single flat table
Converts the joined report back into a matrix report
Applies one shared row grouping field so every block's rows line up
questions.explain: Group Across Blocks sets one field that every block groups by, so each block's data lines up against the same set of rows, making comparison possible.

questions.q: What makes a cross-block summary formula different from a regular summary formula?
options: It only works with text fields
It can reference values from more than one block in the same calculation
It can only be used in a tabular report
It replaces the need for a report type entirely
questions.explain: A regular summary formula calculates within one block. A cross-block summary formula reaches across multiple blocks, such as dividing an amount in one block by a count in another.

questions.q: When is a joined report the right choice over a matrix report?
options: Whenever a report needs more than 5 columns
Whenever a report needs a chart
Whenever the data has fewer than 10 records
Whenever the comparison spans more than one report type or filtered slice that a single block can't hold
questions.explain: A matrix report stays within one report type and one set of filters. A joined report is for when the comparison genuinely needs separate blocks, each with its own type or filters, side by side.
